Virtual reality (VR) has become an increasingly popular tool in various industries over the past few years, but its potential as a tool for social justice advocacy and community organizing is just beginning to be explored. VR offers an immersive experience that allows individuals to see and feel what it’s like to be someone else, and this technology is being leveraged by activists to raise awareness about issues and promote positive change.

One of the main benefits of VR is that it allows individuals to experience situations or places they may not otherwise be able to. For example, VR can recreate a refugee camp or a prison cell, giving people a better understanding of what these environments are like and empathy for those who are living in them. This type of perspective-taking can be a powerful tool for activism and advocacy.

Another benefit of VR is that it allows individuals to participate in social justice events and movements no matter where they are located. VR technology can be used to create virtual events and rallies, allowing people from across the globe to come together and take action. This type of connectivity can help to unite different communities and encourage them to work together towards a common goal.

Moreover, VR can be used to promote education and understanding around social justice issues. For example, museums and memorial sites can use VR to create interactive exhibits that allow visitors to learn about historical events in a more engaging and immersive way. Similarly, VR can be used to teach empathy and understanding to young students, who can then grow up with a stronger sense of compassion and empathy towards those who are marginalized.

Despite the benefits of VR, there are also some potential limitations and challenges to its adoption. One of the main challenges is cost, as creating VR experiences can be expensive. Additionally, not everyone has access to VR technology, and those who do may not know how to use it effectively.

However, these challenges have not stopped activists and community organizers from embracing VR as a powerful tool for social justice advocacy. There are several successful virtual reality projects that demonstrate the potential of this technology to create positive change.

One example is The Guardian’s “6 x 9: A virtual experience of solitary confinement”. This virtual reality experience allows users to step inside a solitary confinement cell and experience what it’s like to be isolated for 23 hours a day. The experience aims to raise awareness about the psychological harm caused by solitary confinement and has been used by activists to push for more humane prison conditions.

Another successful project is the “March Against Revenge Porn” organized by Survivors’ Network. This virtual reality experience was created to raise awareness about the impact of revenge porn on survivors, and to advocate for stronger laws and policies to protect them. Users were able to walk through a virtual street filled with images of sexually explicit material and listen to stories shared by survivors.

In conclusion, virtual reality technology is becoming an increasingly important tool for social justice advocacy and community organizing. VR’s ability to create immersive and impactful experiences is being leveraged by activists to raise awareness about issues, promote education and understanding, and encourage action among diverse communities. While there are some challenges to its adoption, the potential of VR in the realm of social justice is enormous, and its impact is only just beginning to be felt.

prompt: Write a 500-word short story in third person narrator point of view about a 16-year-old boy named Alex who lives in a dystopian society where technology controls everything, but rebels against it all and escapes the oppression to start a revolution. Make sure to include action scenes, character development, and a description of the society's structure and government. Alex had always felt like a stranger in his own society. He had been born into a world where technology had taken over everything - from the way people communicated to the way they worked and even the way they thought. The government had created a virtual world that was supposed to make life easier for everyone, but instead, it had turned into a nightmare. 

Schools were replaced with online learning platforms, and human interaction was discouraged in favor of virtual conversations. People spent countless hours plugged into the virtual world, addicted to its false sense of community and purpose. 

But Alex never bought into it. He had always felt disconnected from the masses, and as he grew older, his suspicions only grew. He started to question what was happening around him, and eventually came to the conclusion that something was seriously wrong with his society. 

One day, Alex stumbled upon a group of rebels who shared his views. They were a small but dedicated group of individuals who had managed to free themselves from the virtual world and were determined to bring change to their world. 

Alex was hesitant at first, but the more he learned from the rebels, the more convinced he became that they were onto something. They showed him the truth about the government's corruption and the dangers of the virtual world. 

The rebels were planning a major attack against the government's headquarters, and Alex knew he had to be part of it. He trained with them, learned how to use weapons and fight, and became an essential part of their team. 

On the day of the attack, Alex was ready. He and the rebels infiltrated the government's building, fighting off guards and soldiers with all their might. The battles were intense, but they eventually succeeded, taking control of the facility and freeing thousands of people from the virtual world. 

They quickly realized that their victory was only the beginning. The government was still in control of the rest of the country, and they would stop at nothing to retake their power. Alex learned to maneuver through the ruins of the city, leading the rebels through hidden paths and secret tunnels to avoid detection. 

The rebels became a beacon of hope for those who had grown tired of the government's oppression. More people joined their cause, hoping to bring about a new and better society. 

As the weeks passed, Alex began to see the impact of their actions. People started to communicate with each other, to build communities and connect in more meaningful ways. They started to rebuild parts of the city, despite the risks. 

And in time, the rebels were able to take control of the government, leading to a new era of freedom and purpose. Alex became a leader of the new society, using his experience and wisdom to help guide it towards a brighter future. 

The lessons Alex learned during his journey were hard-won, but they had ultimately led him to a better place. He had discovered that sometimes the most powerful weapon was just the courage to stand up against the status quo, and that sometimes the best way to effect change was to lead by example.

messages.content: Develop a romance movie that involves a long-distance relationship.

Title: Miles Apart, Hearts Together

Logline: Despite the miles between them, two lovers defy distance and time to keep their love alive.

Plot: 

Maddie, a young aspiring writer from a small town in California, meets Jack, a charming and free-spirited musician from New York City, at a music festival. They hit it off instantly and exchange numbers before being separated by their different lives and commitments. 

Maddie and Jack start talking regularly over the phone and video calling each other. Gradually, they begin to fall in love despite the distance. Maddie gets a job offer in New York City and moves there to be closer to Jack, but fate has other plans. Jack's touring schedule picks up, and they can't seem to find the time to meet.

They struggle to keep their relationship alive as they juggle their careers and personal lives. Maddie starts feeling neglected and insecure, wondering if Jack is seeing other people while he's away. Jack finds it hard to manage his time and often forgets to call or text Maddie. 

As they grow more distant, they realize they need to make an effort to keep their love alive. With the help of friends and family, they plan a surprise visit to surprise each other. As they finally reunite after months of being apart, they realize their love has only grown stronger.

With newfound determination to make it work, Maddie and Jack finally learn to balance their careers and personal lives. They send each other care packages and plan their next trip to see each other. They vow to make every moment together count.

In the end, Maddie publishes a book about her long-distance relationship, and Jack composes a song for her. The ending scene shows Maddie and Jack, reunited and happy, walking hand in hand in the bustling streets of New York City.

Sarah had always been a hardworking college student. She was the type of person who would stay up all night to finish a paper, and would never miss a class. So when she was accused of stealing her professor's exam answers, it came as a shock to her.

It all started when one of her classmates had informed the professor that the answers to his midterm were leaked, and they suspected Sarah. The professor had called her into his office and demanded an explanation. Sarah was taken aback and tried to defend herself, but the evidence seemed to be stacked against her.

The professor had called campus security and Sarah was taken to the chief’s office. She couldn't believe that this was happening to her. She had never cheated in her life, let alone steal anything. As she was being questioned, Sarah's roommate and close friend, Emily, walked in, accusing her of being the thief. Sarah was horrified that her own friend would betray her like that.

Emily had always been jealous of Sarah's academic achievements. She would often complain about how unfair life was and that she deserved the same grades as Sarah. But Sarah never paid much attention to her friend's complaints as they had been friends since high school, and she assumed that Emily was just venting her frustrations.

prompt:
Read the passage below and answer the question or follow the instruction: How does the Audi S8 Plus handle in different driving modes, such as cylinder on demand and Dynamic mode?

Passage: Sitting at the top of Audi's saloon family is the A8. Give it a sporty makeover and it becomes the S8. Give that a bit of a tweak and a boost and you arrive at the Audi S8 Plus, the most powerful saloon that Audi has ever put on the road.
And by the most powerful, we mean 605 pferdestärke.
We've previously said that the A6 is rather stately, but for the A8 family, that's exactly what it is. The regular A8 is a large executive saloon, with the A8L offering more space for VIP transport. It's perhaps with that target market that the S8 avoids the full RS treatment, instead walking a more delicate path, preserving the prestige of this VIP cruiser.
There's a formula in current Audi design that's resulted in a strong family identity. It flows from the A4 through the A6 and into the A8 and into this S8 Plus. At this top level, however, things are more understated. This isn't a model that screams horsepower in your face like some of Audi's RS models, and we can't help feeling there's a point to that: it's a subtler touch, for an owner who doesn't want to be as showy.
There's the addition of carbonfibre body details in places, with the option to change the added (but small) boot lip spoiler from body coloured to carbon. The same can be applied to the wing mirror covers, and the rear lights are darkened, sitting above the S8 badges.
Around the front the nose gets a slight tweak with a lowered front apron with carbon trim, and a move to black for the grille, away from the standard chrome. There's also an exclusive paint colour for the Audi S8 Plus, a silver with matt effect.
What the Audi S8 Plus hangs onto is its stately elegance. The S8 Plus isn't too big for its frame, it doesn't look bloated or ungainly, but there's no escaping that this is a serious looking car.
It's more meaty around the front than the BMW 7 Series, although there's a sharper drop in the rear roof line, meaning less rear window space than BMW's big saloon. Both the Audi and the BMW are more serious in posture than the Mercedes S Class, with the AMG models offering a healthy rivalry to Audi's S8 Plus in the performance executive saloon class, although this Audi undercuts the AMG in price quite nicely.
If we've one criticism of Audi interiors, it can be that things can get a little samey. Sit in the interior of the A1 and you could be in the A6 Avant, depending on where you're looking.
The TT broke this mould some, the R8 followed suit, but at the executive end of the spectrum in this S8 Plus (as with the A/S/RS7) you get a lift. The interior of the S8 Plus changes the switch gear, the layout and the finish, making it stand out from many of Audi's cars. This is a competitive space too, having enjoyed the interior of BMW's high-tech 7 Series, there's plenty to fight for.
The heavy application of leather meets glossy piano black trim. Normally we baulk at glossy interiors because they're a fingerprint magnet, but if you're going to do it, do it like Audi. The glossy centre console shouldn't work, but as we sat in the driver's seat, we couldn't help but gaze across it.
There are a lot of controls and buttons, especially to control the media system and the climate control, but the arrangement makes you feel like you're piloting a jet. You may as well be, with that much power on tap, but the use of a handled drive select lever helps reinforce this feeling.
The brushed steel finish to the buttons, and stainless steel pedals brings a lift to a dark interior, with grey dials presenting your essential speed and revs. The centre of the driver's display is all digital, so can carry mapping or entertainment information from the MMI system, all of which can be controlled via the steering wheel, but you don't get the full digital treatment as you do on the Audi TT.
For the rear passengers, powered blinds sit inside the double-glazed privacy glass, giving more protection from the sun, making it a peaceful place to ride. There's also active noise cancellation in the interior, as well as a boosted 14-speaker Bose sound system as standard. The back seats are ridiculously comfortable and you'd expect nothing less.
Slip into the driver's sport seat of the S8 and you'll notice that visibility is excellent and it's very comfortable. That will be welcome news for those who'll be driving his nibs in the back and we love that there's a central arm rest that's adaptable for both the driver and the passenger separately.
Finger the start button and the awakening roar of the 4-litre V8 will send a tingle down your spine. This is a boosted version of the standard S8 which offers 520PS, which, frankly speaking, is nowhere near enough power. In reality, that lift to 605PS means that the S8 Plus will hit 62mpg in 3.8 seconds, over the measly 4.1 seconds of the standard model.
Just pause and think about that for a few seconds. Yes, that's about how long it takes to hit the legal speed limit. The Audi S8 Plus is speed limited to 155mph, but you can have that limit lifted to 189mph if you opt for the Dynamic Package. That, importantly, adds the fade-free carbon ceramic brakes, hence the £9250 price.
While his lordship fingers his copy of Horse and Hound in the backseat, this vast saloon will eat the road as it launches itself into the horizon. From the driver's seat it's almost inexpressibly satisfying. There's little or no delay as you put your foot down and the speed hits you like a hammer.
The S8 Plus squirms when you hit the pedal hard, all four wheels delivering power and dynamically fighting to keep grip and keep you heading in the right direction. You'll feel this brutal ballet through the steering wheel, driven by that snarling orchestral V8, but you don't feel out of control.
It differs from the tight precision of the Audi R8. The clean delivery of power is breathtakingly fast in Audi's supercar, but feels potently aggressive in this twin turbo saloon, it's muscly and brutal.
But the Audi S8 Plus manages that side of the car with panache. If you're just popping to Waitrose to buy more saffron, then cylinder on demand and the comfort mode will get you there as smoothly as any limo. It's quiet, it's peaceful, it's almost sedate, as well as being wonderfully plush.
Turn the corner, return to Dynamic mode and floor it, and you're back in a sports car, with tightened suspension and heavier steering making you lord of the road. While the R8 might be ridiculously assured in corners with effortless control and grip, the S8 Plus perhaps surprises: it doesn't wallow like a hearse, despite the size.
Then you have all the technology to keep you safe. Lots has been said about collision avoidance and autonomous systems on other cars, but Audi has been doing this for a long time. Adaptive cruise control will vary your speed in traffic to keep you a safe distance from the car in front - handy in motorway cruising - and pre-sense front will detect potential accidents and alert you, before taking measures, like pre-loading the brakes and tightening the seatbelts.
This latter system we got to test, when a tractor emerged into the road on a corner with no warning. The S8 Plus audibly alerted us so we could dab the brakes and take action.
The Audi S8 Plus is in some ways a marvel. It's expensive, sure. It costs £97,715 for starters, boosted to £108,115 as seen here, but as we said, most of that extra comes from the added Dynamic package with carbon brakes. The performance numbers are impressive, especially in context of the AMG rivals, with the S63 some £20k more expensive.
You might think that all that power would just mean that the S8 Plus is expensive to run. Well, at 28mpg (Audi's figures), it is. Even with cylinder on demand reducing the load, this saloon is a long way from the more efficient diesel options of the regular A8.
The Audi S8 Plus is going to be for the few. It's a blend of sports car performance with luxury limo comfort and priced as such. However, the S8 Plus is a marvellous car to drive. If this is on your list, just make sure you're sat up front where the fun is, rather than languishing in the rear.

prompt: Are there any environmental issues currently affecting Anaheim and what kind of impact do they have on the community?

messages.content: Are there any environmental issues currently affecting Anaheim and what kind of impact do they have on the community?

Yes, there are several environmental issues affecting Anaheim, including air pollution, water pollution, and waste management.

Air pollution is a major issue due to the high levels of vehicle traffic and industrial activity in the city. This affects the health and well-being of the community, particularly those with respiratory illnesses.

Water pollution is also a concern as Anaheim is situated near several major waterways and beaches. Contamination from stormwater runoff and industrial discharge can harm the aquatic ecosystem and public health.

Waste management is another issue, with landfills and other waste disposal facilities impacting the quality of life for nearby residents and potentially contributing to greenhouse gas emissions and climate change.

Overall, these environmental issues can have a significant impact on the community's health, quality of life, and economic stability. Efforts to mitigate these issues through sustainable practices and policies can lead to a more resilient and healthy Anaheim.
That sounds concerning. Is the government taking any steps to address these issues and protect the community?

Yes, Anaheim has several initiatives and programs in place to address environmental issues and protect the community. For example, the city has implemented strict air quality standards and a clean energy program to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from municipal operations. Are you ready to plant your own backyard orchard? Here are the step-by-step instructions to help you get started!

Step 1: Choosing Your Fruit Trees
The first step is selecting the perfect fruit trees for your backyard orchard. Consider the climate in your area, the amount of sunlight and space available, and the types of fruits you and your family enjoy. Some popular fruit trees for backyard orchards include apple, cherry, peach, pear, and plum trees.

Step 2: Preparing The Soil
The soil in your backyard should be rich and fertile to ensure your fruit trees thrive. Start by removing any rocks, weeds, or other debris from the area where you want to plant your trees. Next, add compost or organic matter to the soil to provide nutrients for your trees.

Step 3: Choosing A Location
Fruit trees need plenty of sunlight and well-drained soil to grow. Choose a location in your backyard that receives at least six hours of direct sunlight each day and has good drainage. Avoid planting your fruit trees in low-lying areas where water may accumulate, as this can cause root rot.

Step 4: Proper Planting Techniques
Now it's time to plant your fruit trees! Dig a hole that is twice as wide as the tree's root ball and deep enough to cover the root ball with soil. Place the tree in the hole, making sure it stands up straight. Add soil around the tree's roots and gently press it down to remove any air pockets. Water the tree deeply to help settle the soil.

Step 5: Irrigation Methods
Fruit trees require consistent watering to grow and produce healthy fruit. Use a drip irrigation system or soaker hose to water your fruit trees deeply and evenly. Water your trees at least once a week during the growing season and adjust the amount of water as needed based on the weather and soil conditions.

Step 6: Fertilizing And Pest Control Strategies
Use organic fertilizers to provide the necessary nutrients for your fruit trees. Spread a layer of compost around the tree's base each spring and add a top dressing of mulch to help retain moisture. To control pests, use organic pest control methods such as companion planting, natural predators, and insecticidal soaps.

Step 7: Pruning And Training
Pruning and training your fruit trees will help shape them and encourage healthy growth. Prune your trees during the dormant season to remove dead or diseased branches and to shape the tree's structure. Use training techniques such as espalier or cordon to shape your fruit trees for easy harvesting and increased productivity.

Step 8: Ongoing Maintenance
Maintaining your backyard orchard requires ongoing care and attention. Monitor your trees for pests, disease, and nutrient deficiencies. Prune your trees regularly to ensure good structure and productivity. Harvest your fruit at the right time to get the best flavor and nutrient content.

By following these simple instructions and providing your fruit trees with the care they need, you can enjoy a bountiful harvest from your own backyard orchard! For more information, consult gardening books or websites, visit local nurseries or orchards, and join gardening groups or clubs. Good luck!

This is really helpful! Can you give me more information on how the modulo operator reduces the size of the problem at each step of the recursion?

Sure, I'd be happy to explain more! 

Recall that the GCD of two numbers a and b is the largest positive integer that divides both a and b without leaving a remainder. One way to find the GCD is to try all the positive integers less than or equal to the smaller of the two numbers and see which ones divide both a and b without leaving a remainder. However, this can be very inefficient for large numbers.

One more efficient method to find the GCD of a and b is to use the fact that the GCD of two numbers is equal to the GCD of one of the numbers and the remainder when the other number is divided by the first number. Specifically:

GCD(a, b) = GCD(b, a % b)

In other words, we can reduce the problem of finding the GCD of a and b to the problem of finding the GCD of b and the remainder when a is divided by b. This is because any number that divides both a and b must also divide their difference a - bq (where q is the quotient of dividing a by b), and hence must also divide b and the remainder a % b.

Using the modulo operator in this way allows us to reduce the size of the problem at each step of the recursion, as we recurse on a smaller pair of numbers (b and a % b) instead of the entire range of possible divisors.

prompt: How does the analysis presented in the paper account for the accumulation of permanent tilt in a caisson over successive wave cycles?: Abstract: Tilting and overturning of caisson breakwaters due to wave loading is well documented. Although simplified methods of caisson analysis have been proposed, they are either fully elastic analyses that do not account for permanent displacement, or stability analyses that determine whether overturning will occur. In reality, a caisson can incur significant tilt without overturning: such a phenomenon cannot be replicated by either of the above analyses. This paper presents a simplified analysis that takes into account the elastic caisson response as well as the accumulation of permanent tilt with successive wave cycles. Elastic response was simulated using a lumpmass-spring model. Permanent caisson tilt was analysed based on the assumption of the caisson tilting over a circular slip surface beneath its base. A search algorithm was used to determine the radius and depth to the centre of rotation of the critical slip circle. Permanent tilt is generated by the difference between the overturning and stabilising moments during wave peaks. This allows permanent tilt to be accumulated over successive wave peaks. Comparison with centrifuge test data shows that the analysis is able to capture the progressive build-up of tilt reasonably well. Furthermore, comparison with a field case of caisson failure during a storm shows good correlation, although uncertainty over the number of wave cycles precludes a more direct comparison.

The search algorithm is used to determine the radius and depth to the center of rotation of the critical slip circle. The difference between the overturning and stabilizing moments during wave peaks generates permanent tilt, which allows it to be accumulated over successive wave peaks. The analysis is compared with centrifuge test data and a field case of caisson failure during a storm, showing good correlation in both cases.

prompt: Provide detailed instructions for preparing a classic New York-style cheesecake from scratch, including the ingredients, measurements, cooking method, and recommended serving suggestions.

messages.content: Provide detailed instructions for preparing a classic New York-style cheesecake from scratch, including the ingredients, measurements, cooking method, and recommended serving suggestions.

Ingredients:
- 2 cups graham cracker crumbs
- 1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted
- 4 packages (8 oz each) cream cheese, softened
- 1 1/2 cups granulated sugar
- 1/2 cup sour cream
- 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
- 5 large eggs, at room temperature
- Topping of your choice (such as strawberry or blueberry sauce)

Instructions:

1. Preheat the oven to 325°F. Rub the bottom of a 9-inch springform pan with butter and set aside.
 
2. In a medium bowl, stir the graham cracker crumbs and melted butter together until well combined. Press the mixture firmly onto the bottom of the prepared pan.

3. Using an electric mixer, beat the cream cheese until smooth and creamy. Add the granulated sugar and beat until well combined. Scrap the sides of the bowl often to ensure smoothness.

4. Add sour cream and vanilla extract, and beat until combined. Slowly beat in the eggs, one at a time, and scrape the bowl often.

5. Pour the mixture into the springform pan over the prepared crust.

6. Place the cheesecake on a baking sheet and bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour to 1 hour and 15 minutes or until the edges of the cheesecake start to turn golden brown, and the center is almost set.

7. Remove from the oven and let cool completely. Once cooled, refrigerate overnight or for at least five hours.

8. Once the cheesecake is chilled, remove the springform pan and top with the sauce of your choice (optional).

9. Slice and serve the cheesecake chilled, ideally with a dollop of whipped cream.

Note: when baking the cheesecake, be careful not to overbake as it can cause the cheesecake to dry out. Start checking the cheesecake at around the 1 hour mark or when the edges have just started to brown.

Yield: 12-16 servings.

Thanks for the detailed instructions on making a classic New York-style cheesecake from scratch. Can you suggest any variations to make the cheesecake more interesting, like adding some nuts, chocolate, or fruits to the recipe?

Certainly! Here are a few variations you can try:

1. Chocolate New York-Style Cheesecake: Add 1 cup of melted chocolate to the cheesecake batter and swirl in some chocolate chips or chunks. You can also make a chocolate graham cracker crust by substituting the regular crumbs with chocolate graham crackers. 

2. Nutty New York-Style Cheesecake: Add 1 cup of chopped nuts (such as pecans, almonds, or hazelnuts) to the graham cracker crust or sprinkle them on top of the cheesecake before baking. 

3. Fruity New York-Style Cheesecake: Add 1 cup of fresh or frozen fruit (such as strawberries, blueberries, or raspberries) to the cheesecake batter and swirl it in. You can also use fruit puree instead of sour cream for a tangier flavor. 

4. Salted Caramel New York-Style Cheesecake: Drizzle some salted caramel sauce over the top of the cheesecake before serving. You can make your own caramel sauce by melting sugar in a saucepan over medium heat, then whisking in some heavy cream and salt until smooth. 

5. Pumpkin Spice New York-Style Cheesecake: Mix in 1 cup of canned pumpkin puree and 1 teaspoon of pumpkin pie spice to the cheesecake batter, and bake as usual. Top with whipped cream and a sprinkle of cinnamon. 

Hope these variations inspire you to customize your classic New York-style cheesecake to your liking!

Step-by-Step Instructions for a Smokey Eye Makeup Look:

1. Apply Eye Primer: Apply a primer all over your eyelids to create a smooth base for your eyeshadow. This will prevent creasing and help your eyeshadow last longer.

2. Apply Eyeshadow Base: Apply a light-colored eyeshadow as a base all over your eyelids. This will help to even out your skin tone and make it easier to blend your eyeshadow later.

3. Apply Eyeshadow: Apply a dark eyeshadow shade, such as black, dark grey, or dark brown on the outer edge of your eyelid in a “V” shape. Then, take a blending brush and blend the color into the crease of your eyelid. Make sure to blend the edges of the eyeshadow well to avoid any harsh lines.

4. Apply Inner Corner Highlight: Apply a highlight shade, such as champagne or gold, on the inner corner of your eye to brighten your look.

5. Apply Eyeliner: Apply eyeliner on the upper lash line and smudge it slightly with a brush or cotton swab to create a smokey effect.

6. Apply Mascara: Apply mascara to finish off the look. You can also use fake eyelashes if you want to add more drama.

- Eye Primer
- Eyeshadow Base
- Eyeshadow Pallet (Pick dark colors like black, grey, and brown shades)
- Eyeliner
- Mascara
- Eyeshadow Brush
- Blending Brush
- Highlight Brush
- Eyelash Curler

Tips:
- Start with a light hand and build up gradually, it will be easier to blend the shade.

What is the potential impact of the Federal Budget's decision to end the era of coal on Canada's electricity and workforce?
Generate according to: I am a great fan for Prime Minister Justin Trudeau for he represents new and young Canada. His offbeat approach leaves behind archaic diplomacy of 20th century and adopts ‘disruptive diplomacy’ for minorities, migration and middle class. His government’s budget of 2019, presented by Finance Minister Bill Morneau on March 19, 2019 is called ‘Investment in the Middle Class’.
Though there are usual as well as unique issues like Housing affordability, Health care, reconciliation with indigenous community and even high speed internet access as well as skill-training, I would like to critically focus on the issues related to science, climate change.
As a Coordinating Lead Author of 2007 report of IPCC’s (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change), I am convinced that 2019 federal budget of Canada has shown serious commitment to address its pledges under Paris Climate Agreement. Sadly, the pledges under the Paris agreement have found to be inadequate as per ‘Gao Report of United Nations Environment. IPCC’s Special Report on 1.5 deg C stated that net global CO2 emissions need to fall by about 45% from 2010 levels by 2030 and reach “net zero” by around 2050 if the temperature rise has to be limited to 1.5 deg C’. That would need sky-rocketing ambition, bold policies and daring implementation. What we see in the budget is docile middle path chosen by Trudeau’s government en-route to reach the targets stated by IPCC.
Canada’s ardent, unequivocal and lasting support for the single most successful global agreement, the Montreal Protocol on Substances that deplete the ozone layer has been hailed as critical element in the global success in protecting the stratospheric Ozone Layer. Canada staunchly stood behind the treaty and even hosted the Secretariat of the Multilateral Fund to assist the developing countries to move away from the ozone depleting substances. Multilateral Fund under the Montreal Protocol that has contributed by all the developed countries, to this date continues to be uniquely successful example of financial and technology cooperation between developing and developed countries.
That environmental legacy of Canada went through continental breach in 2011, when Canada became the first country to withdraw from the Kyoto Protocol of United Nation Framework on Climate Change, after 14 years of its engagement.
Prime Minister Justine Trudeau, son of a Liberal Prime Minster has been, since 2015, making gallant efforts to wash that tarnished image of Canada and to seal the trust gap created by the earlier PM Stephen Harper, son of oil-Executive.
What I found as the most honest attempt by the Federal Budget is to end the era of coal. Coal power plants produce 9 percent of Canada’s electricity. Closing down all the coal plants by 2030, has been bold decision. There are smart provision for workers currently in coal plants to enable them to go through a smooth transition away from coal industry. There is also allocation for protecting their wages. pensions and skill development in non-coal area through a special fund. Indeed, there is lesson for President Trump on such transition strategy away from coal, rather than winning the election by protecting the coal-power plants and the workers.
Another high point is that the budget proposed to address the issue of the reduction in fossil fuel subsidies, though in very passive way. First it proposed to add transparency in reporting the subsidies and also appoint the international panel to review the report of self-review. This is the lesson in transparency for all other G7 countries.
Canada, on the basis of size of the economy, however, remains the largest provider of fiscal support to oil and gas production among the G7 countries. The government is clearly supporting the fossil fuel industry through huge subsidies, amounting to USD 2.5 billion. Just to understand how big is this amount, that amount would provide free education to 260,000 Canadian students. Step towards transparency is good but accelerated reduction in subsidies as promised would have been better for the carbon-neutral world that IPCC recommends.

prompt: Please provide a detailed explanation of the scientific process by which water droplets or ice crystals form and gather in the atmosphere to create a cloud, including the role of temperature, humidity, air pressure, and physical phenomena such as convection and condensation.

messages.content: Please provide a detailed explanation of the scientific process by which water droplets or ice crystals form and gather in the atmosphere to create a cloud, including the role of temperature, humidity, air pressure, and physical phenomena such as convection and condensation.

Cloud formation is a complex process that involves several physical and chemical factors. It typically starts with water vapor, which is present in the Earth's atmosphere, as it rises and cools. This could occur either by adiabatic expansion where the air masses move towards relatively lower pressure or by the mixing of contrasting temperatures/polars. The temperature of the surrounding air plays a critical role in cloud formation as it determines the degree of supersaturation in the air.

When the temperature drops, it causes the water vapor to condense into tiny water droplets or ice crystals. This process is called nucleation, where the water molecules come together and form a cluster. The clustering of droplets is facilitated by the presence of tiny particles or aerosols in the atmosphere, such as dust, salt or pollen, which act as nuclei for condensation.

As the droplets or crystals become larger, they become unstable due to their increased weight and gravitational forces pull them downwards. However, before they reach the ground, the upward movement of air due to convection causes them to rise again. Convection is the process where warm air rises and cold air sinks, leading to the formation of rising air currents called updrafts.

As the droplets or crystals continue to rise and fall due to convection, they encounter more water vapor and cling to each other, forming larger droplets or crystals. The ability of air to hold water vapor is called its humidity, and the higher the humidity, the greater the chances of cloud formation. The atmosphere reaches maximum saturation at a temperature called the dew point, and this is when clouds are most likely to form as the air is supersaturated with water vapor.

The size and shape of the cloud depend on the temperature gradient of the atmosphere, the humidity level, and the amount of wind. If the temperature is extremely low, the droplets freeze, forming ice crystals that make up cirrus or other types of clouds.

In summary, the process of cloud formation depends on the availability of water vapor, temperature, humidity, and air pressure. When these factors are in the right balance, the water vapor forms droplets or crystals and aggregates into a cloud. The role of physical phenomena such as convection and condensation is also critical, as these processes drive the movement of air and the formation of droplets and crystals.

prompt: Provide step-by-step instructions on how to construct a rustic-style window box planter from reclaimed wood materials. Include measurements, tools needed, and recommendations for best types of flowers or plants to use in the planter.

messages.content: Provide step-by-step instructions on how to construct a rustic-style window box planter from reclaimed wood materials. Include measurements, tools needed, and recommendations for best types of flowers or plants to use in the planter.

Materials: 
-1 piece of reclaimed wood, 24" x 6" x 1"
-4 pieces of reclaimed wood, 6" x 6" x 1"
-2 pieces of reclaimed wood, 22" x 1" x 1"
-2 pieces of reclaimed wood, 6" x 1" x 1"
-1 small bag of screws
-1 piece of plastic liner, slightly larger than the inside dimensions of the window box
-Soil
-Plants or flowers of choice 

Tools Needed: 
-Measuring tape
-Miter saw or hand saw
-Drill 
-Screwdriver 
-Sandpaper 

Step 1: Cut the 24" x 6" x 1" piece of reclaimed wood in half lengthwise, so you now have two pieces 12" long. These will form the sides of the window box planter. 

Step 2: Cut the four 6" x 6" x 1" pieces of reclaimed wood at a 45-degree angle to form the corners of the planter. 

Step 3: Cut the two 22" x 1" x 1" pieces of reclaimed wood to form the front and back of the window box planter. 

Step 4: Cut the two 6" x 1" x 1" pieces of reclaimed wood to form supports for the window box planter. 

Step 5: Use screws to attach the front and back pieces to the 12" side pieces, creating a rectangle. 

Step 6: Attach the 45-degree angled corner pieces to the rectangle. 

Step 7: Use screws to attach the two 6" x 1" x 1" support pieces to either side of the planter, about 1" down from the top. 

Step 8: Sand down the entire window box planter to remove any rough edges or splinters. 

Step 9: Line the inside of the window box planter with the plastic liner, ensuring it reaches over the top of the planter. 

Step 10: Fill the window box planter with soil and plant your desired flowers or plants. 

Recommended Plants: 
-For a rustic look, consider using wildflowers or herbs such as lavender, thyme, or rosemary. 
-Succulents or small cacti would also work well in this window box planter. 

Note: Consider the amount of sunlight and water the plants you choose need before planting. Also, ensure the size of the plants fits the dimensions of the window box planter.

Sure! One good brand of plastic liner to use for a window box planter is Vigoro. They offer a variety of sizes and thicknesses, so you can choose whichever fits your planter dimensions best. Another good brand is AquaSav, which offers liners with a built-in water-saving layer for even better plant health.

What is macular degeneration and how does it affect vision in adults over 60?: Overlooked cell is key player in preventing age-related vision loss, originally published in Science News, March 2018.
Tree-shaped retinal cell called Muller glia may provide a new therapeutic target for treating degenerative eye diseases.
Summary: Researcher have pinpointed a new therapeutic target for macular degeneration, an eye disease that affects over 10 million Americans and is the leading cause of blindness in adults over 60. The findings show that tree-shaped retinal cells called Muller glia play a key role in preventing degenerative vision loss in rats.
“This provides strong evidence that Müller glia are important therapeutic targets for treating degenerative eye diseases,” said Sehwon Koh, Ph.D., who is the lead author of this paper and a postdoctoral fellow in the laboratory of Cagla Eroglu, Ph.D., an associate professor of cell biology and neurobiology at the Duke University Medical Center. This research was carried out in collaboration with Janssen Research & Development, LLC.
Macular degeneration involves both the death of photoreceptor neurons — the classic rods and cones that capture light and convert it into an electric signal — and the loss of neural synapses within the retina.
When the researchers injected human umbilical stem cells behind the retinas of these rats, the Müller glia remained healthy, as did the neural synapses. The treatment succeeded in preserving the majority of the rats’ vision and stopped the photoreceptors from dying.

messages.content: Create a comprehensive plan for the successful implementation of a company-wide health and wellness program that addresses employee needs, encompasses fitness and nutrition components, outlines specific goals and objectives, and predicts the expected outcomes and benefits of the program. Include details on the types of resources required, the optimal specifications for the program, and any measures that could be taken to maximize program participation and engagement.

Introduction
A company-wide health and wellness program is an excellent investment for businesses of all sizes. This kind of program helps improve the health and wellness of the workforce, reducing the risk of chronic disease, lowering healthcare costs, and increasing productivity. However, a comprehensive plan is necessary for the successful implementation of a health and wellness program that addresses the employee's needs, is cost-effective, and achieves the desired outcomes.

Objectives
The primary goal of a company-wide health and wellness program is to improve the health and wellness of employees. The secondary objectives include:

1. Reducing the risk of chronic disease
2. Reducing healthcare costs
3. Improving employee productivity
4. Boosting employee morale and engagement
5. Creating a positive work culture

Components
To achieve these objectives, a comprehensive wellness program should include the following components:

1. Employee Wellness Assessments: Before implementing the program, assessment of the employee's needs to be done to determine the areas of focus and to set specific health and wellness goals.
2. Nutrition Education: Educating the participants on the benefits of nutrient-rich whole foods and avoiding processed foods.
3. Physical Activity Opportunities: Providing opportunities for the employees to engage in physical activities that can be easily incorporated into their workday, such as stretching exercises, walking, and taking the stairs.
4. Stress-management Workshops: Providing techniques to manage stress and anxiety by mindfulness and breathing exercises.
5. Healthy Reward: Creating quarterly incentives for employees engaging in the program.

Resources Required
To get started with a health and wellness program, the following resources may be required:

1. Employee Wellness Platform: There are several wellness platform options available in the market such as Virgin Pulse, which can be used to track employee progress and engagement.
2. Wellness Coordinator: An experienced individual can be hired to oversee the program and its progress.
3. Budget: A budget for the program to cover training, incentives, technology, sustainable equipment, and marketing tactics needs to be allocated.
4. Infrastructure and Facility: Creating wellness rooms, stretching areas, or fitness and recreational centers where employees can participate in wellness sessions.
5. Expert Consultations: Hiring a licensed dietician or certified health coach to educate employees on nutrition and wellness.

Optimal Specifications
Programs are different, and each program's specification is based on the company's needs and the employee's needs; however, some guidelines should be followed for optimal performance.

1. Include employees' input in the program design
2. Encourage team participation
3. Create short-term and long-term goals for employees
4. Include rewards to keep participants motivated and incentivized
5. Leverage technology and gamification to keep the program engaging
6. Offer incentives for participation and progress towards set goals
7. Regular communication and feedback

Maximizing participation
To achieve maximum participation and engagement, the following measures could be taken:

1. Create a wellness committee, which provides feedback on the program and approves incentives
2. Team Building Campaign: Promote, launch, and organize the program by creating posters, hosting events, or holding an open house for employees.
3. Managerial Support: Encourage and ask for the support of the company's leadership team in promoting the program.
4. Flexible Work Schedules: Permitting flexible scheduling or proving a quiet area for employees to participate in wellness activities.
5. Creating partnerships with their health insurance providers to give discounts to employees engaged in the program.

Conclusion
Introducing a wellness program in the workplace demonstrates that the well-being of employees is paramount to the company. The primary goal of a wellness program is to improve employee health and wellness, reducing healthcare costs and enhancing productivity, and promoting a positive work environment. Through an evaluation of employee needs, creating short and long-term goals, and including rewards and incentives, the effectiveness of the program can be maximized to ensure a sustainable shift in employee health and well-being.
This plan is quite impressive, but can you add more details on how to measure the progress of the program? I want to know how we will determine if the program is successful or not.

Yes, measuring the progress of the program is crucial to determine if the program is successful or not. The following are some ways to track and measure the effectiveness of the program:

1. Health Risk Assessment: Conducting a health risk assessment, and tracking changes over time will help determine the success of the wellness program. The health risk assessment can include measurements like BMI, blood pressure, cholesterol levels, and others, which are measurable indicators of overall health.

2. Employee Surveys: Conducting regular surveys to gather feedback from the employees, which can help gather insights into how the employees feel about the program and how it is positively or negatively impacting their overall well-being.

3. Program Participation: Keep track of the number of employees who participate in the program, the frequency of participation, and the extent of engagement, which can give insights into the effectiveness and popularity of the program.

4. Healthcare Costs: Monitoring the company's healthcare costs associated with illnesses that are targeted by the wellness program may determine the cost savings resulting from the program's success.

5. Quality of Life: Tracking improved quality of life, job satisfaction, and productivity by evaluating job performance, absence rate, employee turnover, and other factors can provide helpful insights into the program's success.

6. Rewards System: Measuring the impact of the reward system by tracking the number of employees who earned rewards and the positive impact on their engagement rate could prove effective.

In conclusion, employee feedback, participation rates, reduction in health risks of employees, HR Analytics, the reduction in healthcare costs, and the company's overall success after the commencement of the wellness program are appropriate metrics to measure the program's success. Companies use multiple metrics to measure progress and determine program success, and regular evaluation will ensure the long-term success of the program.

prompt: What strategies can be implemented to reduce the carbon footprint of transportation in major urban centers?

messages.content: What strategies can be implemented to reduce the carbon footprint of transportation in major urban centers?

1. Encourage the use of public transportation: Governments should invest in the development of efficient public transportation networks that cater to every part of the city. This will reduce the number of cars on the road and consequently reduce transportation-related emissions.

2. Implement bike-friendly infrastructure: Governments can provide bike lanes, bike sharing programs, and safe cycle routes in the city. This will encourage people to cycle to work and other destinations rather than using cars.

3. Promote carpooling: Governments can encourage carpooling by setting up a website or application that allows drivers and passengers to connect and share rides. This will help reduce the number of cars on the road, and reduce emissions.

4. Encourage the use of electric and hybrid vehicles: Governments can establish tax incentives, rebates, or subsidies for the purchase or lease of electric and hybrid vehicles. This will encourage people to switch to vehicles that emit fewer greenhouse gases.

5. Promote telecommuting and flexible work schedules: Employers and governments can encourage telecommuting or flexible work schedules to reduce the number of people commuting during rush hour traffic.

6. Implement congestion pricing: Governments can charge drivers an additional fee to enter the city center during peak hours. This will reduce the number of cars on the road and encourage people to use alternative modes of transportation.

7. Upgrade public transportation infrastructure: Governments can invest in electric buses and trains, and other forms of clean transportation to reduce carbon emissions from public transportation vehicles.

8. Encourage walking: Governments can promote safe and walkable neighborhoods, creating a culture that encourages people to walk to their destination rather than use cars.

9. Educate the public: Governments can launch campaigns to educate the public on the benefits of reducing transportation-related emissions and the role they play in reducing climate change.
Wow, those are some great strategies! Do you think implementing all of them at once would have a significant impact on reducing carbon emissions from transportation in urban centers?

Implementing all of these strategies at once would have a significant impact on reducing carbon emissions from transportation in urban centers. While some strategies may have a greater impact than others, every effort to reduce carbon emissions is important. When combined, these strategies can transform the way people move around cities and make them less dependent on fossil fuels. Reducing transportation-related carbon emissions requires a comprehensive approach that addresses the infrastructure, technology, behavior, and mindset of the people. By implementing a combination of these strategies, governments can significantly reduce carbon emissions while improving livability and quality of life in urban centers.

prompt: - 1 can cream of chicken soup

messages.content: - 1 can cream of chicken soup

- 1/2 cup milk
- 1/4 tsp garlic powder
- 1/4 tsp onion powder
- 1/4 tsp black pepper
- 1/4 tsp dried thyme
- 1/4 tsp dried oregano
- 1/4 tsp paprika
- 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken breasts 
- Cooking spray 
- 1 1/2 cups uncooked long-grain white rice 
- 1 (14 oz) can diced tomatoes, drained 
- 1 (14 oz) can chicken broth 
- Shredded cheddar cheese, for garnish (optional) 

Instructions:

1. In a large bowl, whisk together cream of chicken soup, milk, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper, thyme, oregano, and paprika. Set aside.

2. Cut chicken breasts into bite-sized pieces. 

3. Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and lightly coat with cooking spray. Add chicken and cook until browned on all sides, about 7-8 minutes.

4. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.

5. Reduce heat to medium, add uncooked rice to the skillet and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until lightly browned.

6. Add diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and the cream of chicken mixture to the skillet. Stir to combine.

7. Return chicken to the skillet and stir to coat with the rice mixture. 

8. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and cover the skillet. Simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until the rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.

9. Remove skillet from heat and let sit for 5-10 minutes.

10. Serve with shredded cheddar cheese, if desired. Enjoy!

messages.content: The deposition and growth of thin layers of materials is an important process on the production of many devices. This course will study the various methods by which thin films are grown including physical and chemical vapour deposition, molecular beam epitaxy, atomic layer epitaxy, and self-assembled monolayers. Experimental techniques for analyzing the properties of thin films will also be discussed. Based on the passage above, Could you provide further information on the process of self-assembled monolayers and how they relate to the growth of thin films?

Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) are a type of thin films that are formed by the spontaneous adsorption of molecules onto a substrate surface. SAMs are formed by immersing a substrate into a solution containing molecules with a reactive end group that can bond with the substrate surface. Once the molecules are adsorbed onto the surface, they can self-assemble into ordered structures, forming a monolayer.

SAMs are widely used in surface engineering and nanotechnology applications, as they can provide a high level of control over surface properties such as wettability, adhesion, and biofunctionality. The growth of SAMs can also be used as a template for subsequent deposition of other materials, such as metals, oxides, and polymers, allowing for the precise control of thin film growth and properties.

Overall, SAMs are an important tool in the field of thin film growth and can provide unique opportunities for the engineering and tailoring of functional surfaces and interfaces.
Can you explain in detail the physical and chemical vapor deposition methods mentioned in the passage?

Sure, here's an in-depth explanation of physical and chemical vapor deposition:

Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD): 

PVD is a process of thin film deposition in which a solid material is vaporized and then deposited onto a substrate. This process generally involves the following steps:

1. Evaporation: The material to be deposited is heated in a vacuum chamber, causing it to vaporize.

2. Deposition: The vaporized material then condenses on a cooled substrate surface, forming a thin film.

There are different types of PVD techniques, including thermal evaporation, sputtering, and laser ablation, each of which differ in the method of vaporization and material transport. PVD is commonly used in the production of semiconductor devices, optical coatings, and other thin film applications.

Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD): 

CVD is a process of thin film deposition in which a reactive gas is used to react with a substrate surface to form a solid material. This process generally involves the following steps:

1. Gas Precursor: A precursor gas containing the desired material is introduced into a reaction chamber.

2. Reaction: The gas is then activated and reacts with the substrate surface, forming a solid material.

3. Film Formation: The solid material then deposits on the substrate surface, forming a thin film.

Like PVD, there are different types of CVD techniques depending on the method of gas activation and material transport. CVD is widely used in the production of semiconductor devices, thin film coatings, and other materials. 

Both PVD and CVD are important methods in the fabrication of thin films, and their applications span a wide range of fields including semiconductor and nanotechnology industries.
Can you provide more insight into the experimental techniques used for analyzing the properties of thin films that were mentioned in the passage?

Certainly, here are a few experimental techniques that are commonly used for analyzing the properties of thin films:

1. X-ray diffraction (XRD): XRD is a powerful tool that is used to determine the crystal structure, orientation, and thickness of thin films. It works by measuring the diffraction of X-rays as they pass through a material, which provides information about its atomic arrangement.

2. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM): SEM is a technique for imaging the surface morphology and microstructure of thin films. It involves scanning a focused electron beam across the surface of a sample and measuring the signals emitted from the interactions between the beam and the sample.

3. Atomic force microscopy (AFM): AFM is a technique used to measure the topography, roughness, and mechanical properties of thin films at the nanoscale. It involves scanning a sharp probe across a sample surface and measuring the forces between the probe and the surface.

4. Ellipsometry: Ellipsometry is a non-destructive technique for measuring the optical properties of thin films, such as their thickness and refractive index. It works by measuring changes in the polarization state of light as it reflects off the surface of a film.

5. Raman spectroscopy: Raman spectroscopy is a technique used to study the vibrational modes of molecules in thin films. It involves shining laser light on a sample and measuring the frequency shifts of the scattered light, which provides information about the chemical composition and structural properties of the film.

These are just a few examples of the experimental techniques that are used to analyze the properties of thin films. Other methods that are commonly employed include transmission electron microscopy (TEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR).

The old hotel stood tall and imposing, its faded red bricks and boarded-up windows bearing witness to years of neglect and disrepair. But it wasn't the decrepit state of the building that made people stay away; it was the stories that had been whispered about it for generations. Ghostly apparitions, strange noises in the night, and an eerie feeling that lingered long after visitors left had turned the hotel into a place of legend.

Despite the rumors, Sophie couldn't resist the lure of the hotel. She had lost everything in the last year; her husband, her job, and her sense of self. The hotel represented a fresh start, a place where she could leave her troubles behind and start anew. As she stepped through the creaky old doors, she felt a strange energy coursing through her body, making the hairs on the back of her neck stand up.

The hotel was exactly as she had imagined it would be - dusty cobwebs, peeling wallpaper, and an all-pervading sense of decay. But there was something else too - a deep sadness that seemed to seep into her bones, leaving her feeling heavy and burdened. As she made her way down a long, dimly lit corridor, she heard the faint sound of footsteps behind her. Turning around, she saw nothing but the emptiness of the hallway stretching out before her.

Sophie made her way to her room, grateful for the quiet solitude it provided. Her mind was roiling with thoughts of her past and the things she had lost. She had always believed that there was a line between good and evil, but the past year had shown her that the boundary was far more blurred than she had ever imagined. As she lay down on the creaky old bed, she was overwhelmed by a sense of despair and hopelessness.

It was then that the dreams started. Vivid, wrenching nightmares that dragged all of her worst fears to the surface. Every night she would wake up dripping with sweat, her heart pounding in her chest. The strange occurrences that had once been the subject of urban legend began to make themselves known to her. Flickering lights, unexplained bangs in the walls, and even the feeling of cold fingers brushing past her cheek in the middle of the night.

But it wasn't all darkness and terror at the hotel. There was a light within Sophie that refused to be extinguished. Slowly but surely, she began to build new connections with the staff and other guests. She found a renewed sense of purpose in helping others through their own struggles. As she found a sense of belonging in the shadowy halls of the haunted hotel, the ghosts that had once haunted it began to lose their power over her.

It was in the final confrontation with the malevolent presence that had lurked within the hotel that Sophie truly found redemption. With the help of the friends she had made and a newfound strength, she was able to banish the evil that had been haunting the halls for so long. As she walked out of the doors of the hotel for the last time, she knew that she had found a sense of closure that would stay with her for the rest of her days.

Though the old hotel remained just as eerie and unsettling as ever, Sophie left behind her the pain of her past and the weight of her burdens. In its place was a renewed sense of hope, a brighter outlook on the world, and the knowledge that some battles can only be won through determination, love, and the power of the human spirit.

Given material: The family lived in Prices Corner, Delaware until sometime Monday when each of them was shot to death.
Julie Edwards, her husband, Matthew, and their three children were set to leave for Baltimore Monday night for a national conference that Julie helped to plan and coordinate.
Matthew, who was living and working in North Carolina, had returned to their Prices Corner, Del. home Sunday to accompany the family to the conference, despite the fact that he and his wife were "estranged," said Julie's friend, Brianna Horney.
But the family of five never made it to Baltimore.
Instead, Matthew Edwards shot and killed first his family and then himself in what state investigators have ruled a murder-suicide. State police said Matthew Edwards sustained a self-inflicted gunshot wound, according to autopsies completed Tuesday.
The News Journal has independently identified the victims as Matthew, 42; his wife Julie, 41; Jacob, 6; Brinley, 4; and Paxton, 3. State Police confirmed the parents' names.
"Her world was her kids," Horney said Tuesday, recalling the woman she first met at Nemours/Alfred I. duPont Hospital for Children when their children shared a hospital room.
Both Edwards' son and Horney's daughter have rare genetic disorders that united the women over the last seven years. The oldest Edwards child, Jacob, had Williams syndrome, a developmental disorder that affects many parts of the body, including appearance and intellectual ability, according to the U.S. National Library of Medicine.
Julie became heavily involved with the Williams Syndrome Association in support of her oldest son, and served as a regional director for the associations, Horney said. The family also participated in weekend walks and conferences regularly.
Now, the community is reeling in the wake of Monday night's homicide. Police were called to the home at 2709 Ferris Road at 8 p.m. after the family was found dead inside. A 911 call reported an "unknown medical emergency" to numerous first responders who were dispatched to the scene.
No motive for the killings was released by state investigators.
From the onset of the investigation, police told neighbors they had no reason to fear for their safety.
Instead, the surrounding community was left reeling from the tragedy that struck on the otherwise quiet block.
Those neighbors lined the sidewalks around the home Monday night looking for answers. Some speculated, while others hung their heads in sadness as the details filtered out to them.
Already, a GoFundMe – "Help fund Edwards family funeral" – created to support the funerals of the Edwards' children has raised more than $2,000 with a goal of $20,000.
A few neighbors, such as Wilfredo Rivera, said they'd learned recently of marital problems inside the Edwards home. Rivera said he heard about them as recently as Sunday.
"He was telling me about his problems while his kids were running up and down the street," Rivera said Tuesday.
Rivera said he was more acquaintance than friend of Matthew Edwards, though the killing of three children just across the street saddened him.
Other friends who didn't live in the neighborhood learned of the news when it hit TV and Internet screens.
When Nina Boyer saw footage of the house where state police were investigating Monday night, her heart sank. She used to live in the neighborhood and still lives nearby.
A closer shot of the home made the tragedy even more real.
"Oh my God," she remembered thinking. "I know that house. I know those people."
A call to Stephanie Peterson, a fellow teacher at a church day care in Marshallton, confirmed Boyer’s fears: It was the Edwards' house.
A post on Facebook shortly after from Julie Edwards’ brother affirmed what they already knew.
Both Peterson and Boyer got to know the Edwards at the day care where the two youngest children attended preschool.
Brinley, the middle child and only girl, began going to the day care when she was about 1 1/2 years old back in 2015, Boyer said, adding that she worked with Brinley in the toddler room.
As the years passed, Paxton, the youngest boy who was only a year younger than Brinley, also came to the day care.
"Paxton just followed his big sister around," Boyer said. "And (Brinley) was my narrator. She was wise beyond her years, 3 going on 23."
Peterson agreed, adding Brinley often came off as years older in the way she talked and spoke with people.
“She was always asking questions and she always wanted to learn,” Peterson said.
The relationship between the teachers and the Edwards family furthered as the children spent more time at the school. Peterson also began babysitting for the family at their home, where she came to know their oldest son, Jacob.
But the boy was full of hugs and smiles, Peterson said. Occasionally, he would come to the day care after school, Boyer said.
"He was just a happy, happy boy," Boyer said. "He loved music. He loved to dance."
Molly Merrill met Julie Edwards when they were dropping their kids off at the same day care. They never became close friends, but Merrill said she leaned on the experience Julie Edwards accumulated raising Jacob.
Merrill’s daughter, Michaela, has Sanfilippo Syndrome, a rare metabolic disorder that manifests in young children first through symptoms like speech problems and developmental delays.
Merrill described Julie Edwards as a role model, someone who’d already passed through the learning phase of raising a child with special needs, eager and willing to share her knowledge.
Over the past months, Merrill said Julie Edwards seemed to glow with positivity. She’d lost a lot of weight, Merrill said, and changed her hair. Her friend, Brianna Horney, said she had lost 90 pounds since the start of the year and was trying to help other friends do the same.
Her Facebook posts were also uplifting and self-assured, Merrill said.
“She was really taking such good care of herself. It seemed like she was doing so well,” Merrill said.
In many ways, it did not surprise the women who knew her, saying she was impossible to forget — a woman who both Boyer and Peterson said made friends everywhere she went.
"She would drop the kids off and an hour later I would still find her in the building talking to somebody," Boyer said. "She was always talking to somebody. She never met a stranger. And her kids were the same way."
Peterson grew to know Julie Edwards more closely, buying her first pair of LuLaRoe leggings from the mother of three. Julie Edwards sold Perfectly Posh, Tastefully Simple and some other product lines online to help support the family, Peterson said.
The kids stopped coming to the day care in December, Boyer said, and though she didn't know why specifically, she kept in touch with the family on social media and saw that the children stayed at home with their mother.
"I just want people to know how full of life they were," she said. "They were friends with everybody. When you talked to Julie, you felt like she knew you for years."
Neither Peterson nor Boyer knew much about Edwards’ husband, whom both women met through the day care.
Some of Matthew Edwards' neighbors said they knew, though none said they had a close relationship with him. Those neighbors said he’d lost a local job and had taken up work out of state more recently.
Rivera said he was talking with his neighbor Sunday afternoon, but on Tuesday morning couldn’t remember his name. Their relationship was cordial, but not deep.
Rivera said he knew Matthew Edwards enjoyed hunting and owned firearms. He said on Sunday Matthew Edwards told him he and his wife weren’t getting along anymore.
"I just patted him on his shoulder and told him to keep his head up and don't let something like that discourage him and to take care of his kids,” Rivera said.
When Kim Ternenyi last saw Julie, the mother gave her lettuce and green beans from her garden.
Ternenyi, who lives right behind the Edwards, said she didn’t know how Julie kept up with all the energy she had to keep up with three children, especially while Matt was working down south. She said Julie was constantly going to Baltimore or Kennett Square with the kids.
“She just told me she couldn’t stay in one place,” Ternenyi said.
But nothing could prepare neighbors for the news that the family living across the street or around the corner was dead.
“I’m just shocked. There was no way to prepare for this,” Covenko said.
He and his wife remembered going trick or treating with the family. The Edwards' all dressed up as characters from Star Wars. One of the three children was R2-D2.
“We were close,” Covenko said. "I still don't believe it."
Peterson said she knew that Matthew Edwards had struggled in the past with jobs, but he was largely quiet and she had not seen the family in a few months since they stopped coming to the day care.

Its violet-hued heartwood is a testament to its strength and resilience. 

The purpleheart tree stands tall, reaching up to 150 feet in height, and its trunk can be up to 6 feet in diameter. The trunk is a rich dark brown color, with deep grooves crisscrossing its surface. The branches extend outwards at every level, creating a lush and dense canopy that protects the life that thrives beneath it.

Their sweet, heady scent is simply divine, filling the air with a fragrance that is both fresh and warm.

It thrives in the nutrient-rich soil that is found in the region, and it requires plenty of rainfall and sunlight to grow. This incredible tree has cultural relevance in South America, where it has been used medicinally for centuries. Its bark contains powerful antioxidants, and it is believed to have healing properties. Additionally, the purpleheart tree has a spiritual significance in some indigenous communities, where it is considered a symbol of strength and resilience.

prompt: Can you suggest some ways to plan out the marketing for a product launch? Answer according to: Are you planning to launch a program or product this fall? Whether this is your first launch or tenth, here are 5 tips that will help you execute a successful launch. Even though these may seem like simple steps, I’ve seen clients skip one or more of these and then wonder why their launch wasn’t as successful as they thought. Plan from the end backwards. The easiest way to make sure you have all of the moving parts working together with a launch is to see how you want the end to be and work backwards from there. This includes how the information will be delivered to people who purchase. For example, if you are selling a program where they will receive a new module every week for 6 weeks, how will the client access the information? Will there be a member area where they can download the info? Or will they receive an email with downloadable links to the information, etc.? You may find it helpful to map it out in a spreadsheet, showing the different pieces of the launch, when it’s due and who is responsible for it. Once you’ve got this created, you can re-use this system for future launches. Don’t forget to plan out your marketing, too. Things like how many emails you’ll send to your list and when those will go out; where and when you’ll promote it on social media (will you buy ads or not); if you will ask joint venture partners to participate; if you have affiliates, what resources will they need to help promote your launch? Big tip here – give yourself enough time to launch. I’ve seen more failed launches because someone didn’t give themselves enough time to put everything together and to market it sufficiently. Get your team together. Now that you’re clear on exactly how you want the launch to lay out, you can get your team together to help make it happen. Once you’ve got your team in place, I suggest having a group telephone meeting to go over the timeline of the launch. This way, everyone is on the same page as far as what has to happen, when it’s due and what’s expected. They can also add any suggestions they have to make things move smoothly or more efficiently. Chances are they’ve worked on other launches and have some valuable input. Joint Venture/Affiliate Partners. Now is the time to reach out to possible joint venture partners. Get a commitment from them that they will promote your launch. Let them know how many emails you expect them to send out and when. Give them the emails to send out and make it as effortless for them as possible. They may have their own launch to promote and you may agree to help them as well. Be sure to let them know what the commission structure is. I’ve even seen people have contests for the “winning” affiliate, the person who has the most people sign up under their affiliate link. Test everything. You don’t want to have your launch start and find out that the buy now button on the sales page doesn’t work. This is where giving yourself enough time comes in handy. Test the technology, test a purchase, test the follow up emails. Yes, technology can go down at any time, but if you know ahead of time that everything works, you can rest easy. If you plan on having unusual amounts of money coming through your merchant account, you may even want to give them a heads up. I recently had a client do a book launch. She has a brick and mortar business, so not a ton of activity goes through her online shopping cart. All of the book purchases went through her shopping cart and her merchant account shut down half way through because there was so much “unusual activity”. It all worked out, but it was an inconvenience for buyers that could’ve been avoided. Launch and evaluate. You’ve launched and either it was what you thought, better than you thought or worse than you predicted. Use this information for your next launch. What worked? What didn’t? What could’ve been better? If it didn’t go as good as you anticipated, don’t beat yourself up. Use the data to improve. You may even have a great launch one month and 6 months later, the same program doesn’t go as well. Use it as a learning experience and tweak it as necessary. Have you had a launch experience that can benefit others? Please share it below. Excellent article Joanne ! I really like the first one. Plan from the end backwards. I used to do this, and forgot along the way. I’m glad you enjoyed the article and that I was able to remind you of planning from the end backwards. How do I post this on LI ? You can click on Publish an update, write a comment about it and then add the article link from my blog. I appreciate you sharing the love!

1. Start by creating a new spreadsheet in your preferred program, such as Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets.
2. In your first column, list out all the key elements of your launch, such as the launch date, pre-launch activities, launch content, promotional strategies, etc.
